lanes.purpose: Structured server-side diagnostics for route, auth, analytics, AI, and runtime incidents.
lanes.intended_use: Operational incident review and channel-specific warning/error inspection.
non_goals: Latency rollups for every tracked route.
Client-side chart hydration truth.
trust_notes: Supporting observability only; do not treat as stronger truth than the route/runtime source being described.

lanes.purpose: Client-reported admin chart hydration health for dashboard/debug visibility.
lanes.intended_use: Track whether admin chart modules loaded, degraded, or failed in the latest client report.
non_goals: Canonical backend analytics truth.
Route runtime latency or failure sampling.
trust_notes: Client-originated supporting signal; use source data and route health for stronger truth.

lanes.purpose: Tracked route runtime sample health for known high-sensitivity endpoints.
lanes.intended_use: Operational route latency/failure/staleness summary for explicitly tracked endpoints.
non_goals: Arbitrary untracked routes.
General diagnostic event logging.
trust_notes: Canonical operational truth for the tracked route runtime lane only.

lanes.purpose: Derived operational summaries that combine diagnostics, route runtime, chart health, and pipeline signals.
lanes.intended_use: Compact admin/debug rollups for operational triage.
non_goals: Replacing the underlying source lanes.
Treating derived summaries as stronger than source truth.
trust_notes: Derived rollup only; source lanes outrank this summary.

lanes.purpose: Canonical scheduler heartbeat lane for queue lifecycle and active-drop notification jobs.
lanes.intended_use: Detect stale schedulers, failed queue jobs, and missing runtime freshness before user-facing symptoms appear.
non_goals: Replacing queue source-of-truth documents.
Acting as a historical analytics warehouse.
trust_notes: Canonical heartbeat truth for queue scheduler freshness.

lanes.purpose: Structured warning budget lane for degraded, fallback, and failed runtime conditions across client, routes, schedulers, and mirrors.
lanes.intended_use: Track repeated degradation classes that should fail lightweight continuity before a full audit is needed.
non_goals: Replacing the primary runtime source or route contract.
Treating warning records as stronger truth than the source invariant they describe.
trust_notes: Supporting continuity lane only; source runtime/config truth still outranks warning records.

lanes.purpose: Persisted outcome lane for drop activation notification dispatch idempotency and failure tracking.
lanes.intended_use: Verify that every canonical activation attempt produced an explicit notification outcome.
non_goals: Replacing the underlying drop lifecycle source documents.
Serving as a client-facing notification inbox.
trust_notes: Canonical outcome truth for activation notification attempts.

lanes.purpose: Canonical watch-session capture quality lane for replay recovery, flush degradation, close-path misses, and viewer session continuity health.
lanes.intended_use: Detect watch-time/session analytics degradation before historical dashboards or downstream rollups become misleading.
non_goals: Replacing the canonical watch-session documents themselves.
Serving as a client-facing analytics chart.
trust_notes: Canonical watch-session documents remain the stronger truth; this lane summarizes continuity and capture quality from those documents.

lanes.purpose: Client-side hydration continuity signals for route modules that use the shared UI continuity helper.
lanes.intended_use: Detect partial module failure, visible warning fallbacks, and hydration success/failure sequencing before signoff.
non_goals: Replacing route runtime truth.
Acting as persisted analytics history.
trust_notes: Advisory client continuity signal only; repo/runtime source truth outranks it.

lanes.purpose: Client-side self-healing for compact/mobile interaction release when focused inputs or unexpected document locks leave surfaces untappable.
lanes.intended_use: Detect and auto-recover compact/mobile UI lockups sooner, while emitting structured UI diagnostics for later triage.
non_goals: Replacing canonical route or layout fixes.
Acting as a persisted operational warehouse.
trust_notes: Client-side recovery aid only; source layout/runtime truth still outranks the recovery signal.
